subject: McGlynn Middle School Action Plan Dispute
overview: The committee addressed significant teacher concerns regarding the McGlynn Middle School action plan, ultimately voting to develop a new plan collaboratively. Other business included reports on financial literacy and anti-violence grants, vocational school class rankings, and Community Preservation Act funding priorities.

items.title: Approval of Minutes
items.summary: Approved the minutes of September 18 as amended to include specific details regarding student impact from new housing developments.

items.title: Bills and Transfer of Funds
items.summary: Approved bills following inquiries into teacher tuition reimbursement, Northeast Conference fees, and turf field refurbishment costs.

items.title: Vocational and High School Merger Report
items.summary: The committee discussed transcript and class ranking difficulties following the merger, moving to have headmasters present solutions if issues are not resolved immediately. Approved motions to request a report on student co-op placements and to revisit the robotics engineering vocational track.

items.title: McGlynn Middle School Action Plan
items.summary: Teachers from McGlynn Middle School protested an administration action plan they felt misrepresented the school and ignored staff input regarding diversity and student needs. Approved a motion for administration and teachers to collaborate on a new action plan to be presented in one month.

items.title: Credit for Life Grant
items.summary: Received a report on a $5,000 grant from the State Treasurer’s office to fund a student financial literacy fair in January 2018.

items.title: Game Change Anti-Violence Grant
items.summary: Received a report on a $3,000 grant from the New England Patriots Foundation to expand the Mentors in Violence Prevention program across middle and high schools.

items.title: Community Preservation Act Report
items.summary: Representatives from the Community Preservation Committee provided an overview of the program, and school committee members suggested using funds for playground renovations and schoolyard beautification.

items.title: Health and Wellness Fair Report
items.summary: Placed on file a report detailing the second annual Health, Wellness, and Fitness Fair which featured 54 vendors and approximately 200 attendees.

items.title: School Brains Software Training
items.summary: Discussed ongoing staff training for student data software and referred the matter to a Committee of the Whole to address parent concerns regarding class rankings.

items.title: Concussion Law and Experience Report
items.summary: Reviewed a three-year report on student concussions, noting an increase in identified cases across various sports including football, soccer, and cheerleading.

items.title: Legal Updates and New Business
items.summary: Received updates on the Tarabelsi trial and an Open Meeting Law ruling regarding Chapter 74 advisory committees, and passed a resolution of condolence for D.L. Velie.
